title: gen-8 first real docket: case C-002 decides which claim-ordering consequence the first dispatch consumer attaches (PR-061, PR-060 c5/c6)
description: Run the first assembly docket under the hardened guards and dispose it as a precedent record. Panel: the five warrant-issued non-clerk names in .harness/roster.json (registro-a, registro-b, revision-doctrina, revision-ataque, revision-mecanismo). Each name MUST be driven by a separate agent context that never sees another panelist's ballot before casting its own; priors are formed independently; the discussion round is sequential in speaker order with each speaker reading the dossier so far. Question for precedent.py case open (--task T-424): 'Under PR-061 as cured by RAT-01, which claim-ordering consequence does the first consumer of reputation.py dispatch attach in blackboard.py, and how does it treat ties, unranked identities and a closed gate?' Alternatives: ADVISORY (next/status print the recommended order; no verb binds), YIELD-AT-NEXT (next reports yield with a distinct exit code when the requester is outranked by a live candidate; claim stays first-come), DEFER-AT-CLAIM (claim refuses for one bounded window when a higher-ranked live candidate exists, with a named refusal event). Common floor stated in the proposal text: ties and unranked identities fall back to (priority, id); a closed gate or any dispatch refusal keeps today's order with a printed reason; the consumer writes nothing reputation.py owns; identity stays self-asserted and the rename bypass is documented, never hidden; PR-060 c5 doubt resolves toward constitutional, so no alternative may key on identity attributes beyond the Phase B score. Sequence: precedent.py case open -> deliberate.py propose --proposer registro-a --case C-002 -> sponsor by two other non-clerk names -> prior by every panelist -> schedule --speakers (all five) -> discuss: every panelist, one contribution per EFFECTIVE alternative, in speaker order -> vote by every panelist -> conclude --method schulze --by registro-b. Then publish the disposing record with precedent.py publish --case C-002 --agent registro-a (issued registro/author seat, not a clerk): ratio equals the tally winner verbatim, --follows PR-061 and PR-060 (typed), --sources including the dossier D-NNN and .harness/operator-rulings-2026-08-22.md (RAT-01), tier with evidence T-424, scope/revisit/validity conditions per T-405, --code-version, operation determination. Record the dossier id, the record id, the NO-DELIBERATION-OBSERVED flag state and the timing (case open to publish, wall clock) in the handoff note. Never fabricate discussion; if the panel produces identical priors and ballots the flag fires and that is the honest outcome. Standing rules: claim with blackboard.py claim <ID> --agent <you>; lock every file you edit with lock.py acquire; no emojis; nothing tracked may contain user paths, sibling-project names or personal tooling; never sign anything; never touch .harness/keys, trust/, constitutional/; never route around prevent_data_loss.py; commit is done by the coordinator, not you; hand off with blackboard.py handoff <ID> --agent <you> --to-role verifier with replayable evidence (exact commands + expected output). A crash is not a refusal: fail closed with a named reason.
